paragraphs: A treadmill is a machine for staying in one place, and everything difficult about it is underneath: a belt that has to move smoothly under a body weight landing on it repeatedly, on a deck that absorbs the impact without feeling soft.

The model holds 147,502 polygons and 153,084 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured generously with 35 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $49 it suits gym and fitness visualisation, equipment marketing, interior and architectural scenes, e-commerce imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2019.
Small floor machines exist for the spaces the big ones cannot reach. Around tables, behind doors, in a corridor that turns twice: the compact size is not a compromise, it is the entire specification.
The model is light at 24,675 polygons and 27,528 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so it drops into any interior. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits facilities and cleaning equipment visualisation, retail and commercial interiors, equipment marketing, training material, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2024.

Foil pouches solved a problem glass and cardboard never could: a barrier against light, air and moisture that weighs almost nothing and folds flat before it is filled. Almost every convenience food category depends on it.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the packaging as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 the set suits packaging design and product visualisation, label mockups, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

An LPG dispenser looks like a petrol pump and works nothing like one. The fuel is under pressure, the coupling locks onto the vehicle rather than being held, and the whole cabinet is built around not letting go until the transfer is finished.
The model holds 76,962 polygons and 76,946 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits fuel station and infrastructure visualisation, equipment marketing, street and architectural scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

A command console is furniture pretending to be a spacecraft. The chair and the desk are one object, the screens curve around a single seated position, and the whole thing is designed so that a character can be shown in control without saying anything.
The model is very light at 6,800 polygons and 7,656 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so several fit in one room. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits science fiction film and animation, game environments, concept art, technology presentation, exhibition work and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

This is a shotgun designed by people who normally design consumer electronics: a smooth shell over the mechanism, a screen on the receiver and an aesthetic borrowed from sports equipment. It was widely mocked and is genuinely interesting as an object.
The model holds 186,265 polygons and 95,356 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in green, and carries StemCell certification.
At $49 it suits game weapons, concept and industrial design illustration, film props, defence presentation, simulation and editorial work. On sale since 2023.

Motocross boots are hinged armour. The ankle is deliberately restricted in one axis and free in another, because the injuries the sport produces are twisting ones, and the buckles exist so the boot can be got off over a broken leg.

The model holds 150,142 polygons and 166,266 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 26 maps, 22 at 4096x4096, 3 at 2048x2048 and one at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 it suits footwear and sports equipment visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, character accessories, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

A rack is a standard that outlived the equipment it was invented for. Nineteen inches wide, measured in units of height, and unchanged since the telephone exchange, which is why almost every piece of professional hardware still fits one.

The model holds 227,722 polygons and 231,157 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps, 2 at 4096x4096 and 5 at 2048x2048, in a generic scheme with no branding. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a second build is offered separately.
At $49 it suits data centre and IT visualisation, hardware marketing, technical documentation, office and server room scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2016.

The V1 was the first cruise missile, and it announced itself. The pulsejet made a sound people learned to listen for, and the moment it cut out was the moment the weapon began to fall, which is a detail no later design ever repeated.
The model is light at 16,507 polygons and 17,692 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 it suits historical and documentary visualisation, museum and exhibition work, period film and television, education material, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Glass awards are engineered around one moment: the photograph of somebody holding one. That is why they are heavy for their size, why the edges catch light, and why the engraving is placed where a camera will find it.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the trophies as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 the set suits corporate and event visualisation, product and e-commerce imagery, award ceremony scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Character design for young children is a discipline of subtraction. Round shapes, no sharp edges, features large enough to read on a small screen, and a pose that carries the emotion without needing the face to be visible at all.
The figure is light at 33,344 polygons and 17,182 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in a happy pose, and carries StemCell certification.
At $49 it suits animation and children's media, game characters, toy and merchandise visualisation, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A set of clubs is a series of the same idea at fourteen different angles. The loft of the face and the length of the shaft are the only real variables, and everything else in the design exists to make those two feel consistent from one club to the next.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the clubs as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 the set suits sports equipment and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, advertising, course and club scenes, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

An asymmetric tread is two tyres in one carcass. The outer shoulder is built for cornering and the inner for water clearance, which is why these tyres are marked for which way round they go and why fitting one backwards ruins both jobs.

The model holds 40,225 polygons and 40,454 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the tyre together with the brake and suspension components. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits automotive engineering and product visualisation, tyre and parts marketing, technical illustration, configurators, game assets and editorial work. On sale since 2025.

The Phalanx is a machine that decides on its own. Radar, gun and control are in one mounting, and once switched to automatic it tracks and engages incoming threats faster than a human could confirm what they are, which is the only way the system works at all.
The model is light at 29,591 polygons and 32,230 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 it suits naval and defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.
